column1: What are the six sequential stages of the browser Critical Rendering Path (CRP)?
column2: 1. DOM Tree construction, 2. CSSOM Tree construction, 3. Render Tree creation, 4. Layout (Reflow), 5. Paint (Rasterization), 6. Compositing.

column1: What is the mathematical formula for Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) in Core Web Vitals?
column2: CLS = Impact Fraction * Distance Fraction (measuring the visual instability of unsized elements during page load).

column1: What is the target threshold for Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) to achieve a "Good" Core Web Vitals score?
column2: CLS <= 0.10 (with high-performing production sites targeting <= 0.05 or 0.00).

column1: How does the CSS property aspect-ratio: 16 / 10 eliminate Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) for dynamic images?
column2: It reserves the exact rectangular box dimensions in the Layout tree before the image bytes download, preventing layout reflow when the asset finishes loading.

column1: What is the definition of Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) in Core Web Vitals?
column2: The timestamp when the largest visible content element (hero image, block of text, or video poster) is fully rendered in the viewport.

column1: What is the target threshold for Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) for a fast user experience?
column2: LCP <= 2.5 seconds on standard 4G mobile networks (targeting <= 1.8s for optimal performance).

column1: What is the definition of Total Blocking Time (TBT) in browser performance profiling?
column2: The total amount of time between FCP and Time to Interactive (TTI) where the browser main thread was blocked by tasks taking longer than 50ms.

column1: How does zero-framework vanilla JavaScript minimize Total Blocking Time (TBT)?
column2: It eliminates the execution of heavy framework hydration, virtual DOM diffing, and runtime library parsing, keeping main thread tasks far below 50ms.

column1: What is the minimum WCAG 2.1 AA color contrast ratio required for normal body text (<18pt or <14pt bold)?
column2: A minimum contrast ratio of 4.5:1 against its background.

column1: What is the minimum WCAG 2.1 AA color contrast ratio required for large text (>=18pt or >=14pt bold) and active UI component boundaries?
column2: A minimum contrast ratio of 3.0:1 against adjacent colors.

column1: What is the mathematical definition of relative luminance (L) under WCAG 2.1 specifications?
column2: L = 0.2126*R + 0.7152*G + 0.0722*B, where R, G, B are normalized and gamma-expanded sRGB color components.

column1: What is the formula to compute the contrast ratio between two colors with relative luminances L1 and L2 (where L1 > L2)?
column2: Contrast Ratio = (L1 + 0.05) / (L2 + 0.05).

column1: What is the minimum recommended touch target dimension under WCAG 2.1 Success Criterion 2.5.5?
column2: 48px by 48px (or 44px by 44px minimum under WCAG 2.2 AA) to prevent touch interaction errors on mobile devices.

column1: What is the purpose of the CSS :focus-visible pseudo-class compared to the standard :focus pseudo-class?
column2: :focus-visible applies focus styling only when the browser determines keyboard navigation is active, eliminating unnecessary focus rings on mouse clicks.

column1: How does an accessible "skip link" operate in semantic HTML5 and CSS?
column2: It is placed as the first focusable child in <body> (<a href="#main-content">), hidden off-screen until focused via Tab, allowing keyboard users to bypass repetitive header navigation.

column1: What does a monotonic heading hierarchy mean in semantic HTML document architecture?
column2: Headings progress sequentially without skipping levels (e.g., <h1> followed by <h2>, and <h2> followed by <h3>), preserving a logical outline for assistive technologies.

column1: What is the Accessibility Object Model (AOM) in modern browser engines?
column2: The parallel internal tree created by the browser from semantic HTML and ARIA attributes that exposes roles, states, and properties directly to OS screen readers.

column1: How does native HTML loading="lazy" optimize browser performance?
column2: It defers the network fetch and decoding of off-screen images until they scroll within a predetermined distance from the active viewport.

column1: What layout shift issue does the CSS property scrollbar-gutter: stable prevent?
column2: It reserves space for the vertical scrollbar regardless of whether content overflows, preventing content jumping horizontally when scrollbars appear or disappear.

column1: Why do CSS transform and opacity animations run at 60/120 FPS without triggering layout or paint?
column2: They are handled entirely on the GPU Compositor thread, bypassing the CPU-bound Layout (Reflow) and Paint passes of the Critical Rendering Path.

column1: What does font-display: swap accomplish in a Google Fonts stylesheet link?
column2: It instructs the browser to immediately render text using a system fallback font, then swap in the custom web font once downloaded, eliminating Flash of Invisible Text (FOIT).

column1: What network handshakes are initiated early by <link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin>?
column2: The browser preemptively completes the DNS lookup, TCP 3-way handshake, and TLS negotiation with the font origin before the CSS requests the font file.

column1: Why does centralized Event Delegation on document.body improve memory efficiency over per-node event listeners?
column2: It allocates a single listener function in the heap (O(1) memory) rather than creating thousands of separate closures and event listener handles across individual DOM nodes.

column1: What security vulnerability does rel="noopener noreferrer" prevent when using target="_blank"?
column2: Reverse Tabnabbing: it prevents the newly opened window from accessing and hijacking the origin window's location via window.opener.

column1: What is the browser effect of setting overflow-x: hidden on the <body> root element?
column2: It suppresses horizontal scrollbars and clips unintentional micro-overflow caused by margin collapse, absolute positioning, or fluid sizing on mobile viewports.
